Hi Rishi,

Thanks for the quick demo last week — things are looking promising. Before we proceed with the pilot, our compliance team needs clarity on how Redwood will handle log retention and backup purge phasing for our workspace. Two specific asks from our side:

1) Short-term minimization: We need error/diagnostic logs reduced to a 60-day retention window for standard accounts to reduce PII exposure surface.
2) Forensic carve-outs: For accounts under regulatory review (we expect ~12 active enforcements next quarter) we need an ability to apply a 12-month retention hold on specified logs and retain associated backups. This must be auditable.

Other notes:
- Cross-border backups: we operate primarily in US but have EU customers; any purge/restore operations must respect region-specific holds.
- DPA alignment: please provide a redline or confirmation that the DPA will accommodate these carve-outs and the subprocessor list you are using for backup storage and snapshots.
- Evidence & timelines: attached is our proposed backup timeline and a short questionnaire from legal. Can you review and confirm feasibility?

Attachments: nimbus-backup-timeline-proposal.xlsx, nimbus-dpa-request.pdf

Appreciate it — aiming to lock this before contract signature.

Best,
Sanjay Patel

Hi Sanjay — thanks for the clear ask and for sending the timeline. Quick summary of what we can offer and a proposed execution plan: 

Summary of controls we can put in place
- Tiered retention policy: error/diagnostic logs default to 60 days for standard accounts; operational traces and embeddings follow separate tiering (30/90/365 as appropriate).
- Legal-hold API: we support per-account legal holds that override retention and keep backups immutable for the hold duration. Holds are auditable via the Console (audit log + export).
- Cross-border guardrails: region-tagged backups and purge pipelines — we can pin EU customer backups to EU regions and run purge workflows per-region to obey local holds.

Proposed next steps (timeline):
1) This week: Redwood shares a redline of the DPA and a subprocessor census (we'll attach our redline).
2) Week of Jun 14: Ops run a dry run of the purge pipeline in a sandbox (canary) in the US region; we'll include live monitoring and an abort path.
3) Week of Jun 21: Pilot for 3 Nimbus test accounts with forensic hold toggled; review logs/audit exports; confirm for contract signature.

Open questions from our side:
- Are there any subprocessor snapshot retention SLAs that would force us to keep backups longer than 60 days for certain storage classes? (Marcus, can you confirm?)
- Kimberly, legal will want explicit language for the per-account hold and the audit trail — can we provide sample contract language?

I've attached a draft Redwood DPA response that addresses the hold and audit capabilities. If that looks good, we can proceed to incorporate your redlines.

Attachments: redwood-dpa-response.pdf

Action items:
- Rishi: coordinate sandbox dry run and share monitoring dashboard link.
- Marcus: confirm subprocessor snapshot retention ceilings by Jun 10.
- Kimberly: prepare suggested DPA language for per-account hold and backup carve-outs.

Thanks — will loop in Product if any infra constraints show up during the dry run.

Folks — looping in a few legal/ops notes after skimming Sanjay's packet and Rishi's plan. Key points for contract language and operational confirmation: 

1) Subprocessor ceilings: We need a clear statement in the DPA that disclaims any automatic longer retention due to cold-storage vendor archival policies. If a vendor snapshot lifecycle enforces 180-day retention, we must surface an alternative (export/escrow or different storage class) for Nimbus.

2) Escrow / evidence: For the 12-month forensic carve-outs, legal prefers an escrow-style export capability (encrypted export + manifest) rather than relying on vendor immutability alone. This will be documented as an Ops playbook attachment in the contract.

3) Audit trail format: Confirmed — our Console audit exports include event timestamp, actor, action, resource id, retention override reason. We'll provide a sample export to Nimbus legal.

I've attached the current subprocessor census for snapshot/backup providers; this will be the input for the vendor-side conversation. Marcus, please validate retention ceilings and any migration paths by Wed (Jun 10).
